1	# PYPL Programming Language Popularity Index — April 2026
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	
     5	The PYPL (PopularitY of Programming Language) Index measures how frequently programming language tutorials are searched on Google worldwide. Because it captures learning intent rather than existing web-page counts, PYPL serves as a **leading indicator** of language adoption. The raw data is sourced from Google Trends and normalized so that all language shares sum to 100%, smoothed over a six-month window.
     6	
     7	As of April 2026, **Python commands 36.21%** of all tutorial searches globally, reinforcing its position as the dominant language for the fourth consecutive year.
     8	
     9	## Top 10 Languages — Worldwide Rankings
    10	
    11	| Rank | Language | Share | 1-Year Trend |
    12	|------|------------|--------|-------------|
    13	| 1 | Python | 36.21% | +5.7% |
    14	| 2 | C/C++ | 13.21% | +6.2% |
    15	| 3 | Java | 10.01% | -5.4% |
    16	| 4 | R | 6.17% | +1.6% |
    17	| 5 | JavaScript | 5.07% | -3.0% |
    18	| 6 | Swift | 3.15% | +0.8% |
    19	| 7 | C# | 3.00% | -3.0% |
    20	| 8 | Rust | 2.98% | -0.1% |
    21	| 9 | PHP | 2.96% | -0.7% |
    22	| 10 | Objective-C | 2.57% | +0.1% |
    23	
    24	Python alone accounts for more than a third of all programming tutorial searches, nearly triple the share of its closest competitor.
    25	
    26	## Biggest Gainers and Losers
    27	
    28	The most dramatic year-over-year movement belongs to **C/C++**, which surged **+6.2 percentage points** to claim the #2 spot at 13.21%. Python also grew strongly at +5.7%. On the declining side, **Java fell 5.4 points**, dropping to just above 10%, while **JavaScript** and **C#** each shed 3.0 points.
    29	
    30	Over a five-year horizon, the picture is even starker: **C/C++ gained +7.0%** cumulatively, the largest long-term increase of any language, while **Java lost -7.0%**, the steepest long-term decline.
    31	
    32	## Emerging and Noteworthy Languages
    33	
    34	Beyond the top 10, several languages show interesting trajectories:
    35	
    36	| Language | Share | 1-Year Trend | Note |
    37	|----------|-------|-------------|------|
    38	| Ada | 2.51% | +1.1% | Strong growth in safety-critical domains |
    39	| R | 6.17% | +1.6% | Data-science demand continues |
    40	| Julia | 0.73% | +0.4% | Steady rise in scientific computing |
    41	| Go | 0.71% | -1.3% | Notable decline despite cloud-native popularity |
    42	| Kotlin | 0.90% | -0.9% | Declining despite Android backing |
    43	| Zig | 0.24% | +0.0% | Niche but stable systems language |
    44	
    45	Rust holds steady at 2.98% (essentially flat at -0.1%), maintaining its position just outside the top 7 but not experiencing the explosive growth some predicted.
    46	
    47	## Methodology in Brief
    48	
    49	PYPL exports Google Trends CSV data and processes it with Python's pandas library. Each language's tutorial search interest is measured relative to Java tutorials each month, then normalized to 100%. A six-month smoothing window reduces noise. Unlike the TIOBE Index, which counts existing web pages (a lagging indicator), PYPL focuses on **search intent** — what developers are actively trying to learn — making it a forward-looking measure of language momentum.
    50	
    51	## Key Takeaways
    52	
    53	- **Python is unchallenged at #1** with 36.21% share and still growing.
    54	- **C/C++ is the breakout story of 2026**, posting the largest gains both year-over-year (+6.2%) and over five years (+7.0%).
    55	- **Java's long slide continues**, losing 5.4 points in a single year and 7.0 points over five years.
    56	- **JavaScript and C# are under pressure**, each dropping 3.0 points year-over-year.
    57	- **R and Ada are quiet gainers**, reflecting sustained demand in data science and safety-critical engineering respectively.
    58	
    59	*Data: PYPL / Google Trends, April 2026. © Pierre Carbonnelle, CC BY 3.0.*

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate a portrait data-report poster for the PYPL Programming Language Popularity Index — April 2026.
Dark-mode, developer-aesthetic infographic using Pillow.
"""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Palette & dimensions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
BG = "#0B1120"          # deep navy/charcoal background
PANEL = "#111827"       # slightly lighter panel background
ACCENT_BLUE = "#38BDF8" # electric blue
ACCENT_GREEN = "#34D399"# bright green for gains
ACCENT_RED = "#F87171"  # warm red for losses
TEXT_MAIN = "#F8FAFC"   # near-white headings
TEXT_MUTED = "#94A3B8"  # slate-400 secondary text
TEXT_DIM = "#64748B"    # slate-500 tertiary text
BORDER = "#1E293B"      # subtle border

W, H = 1080, 1920       # portrait canvas (9:16ish)
MARGIN = 60

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Font helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def get_font(size, bold=False, mono=False):
    """Return a TrueType font if available, else default."""
    try:
        if mono:
            return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf", size)
        if bold:
            return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf", size)
        return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf", size)
    except Exception:
        try:
            return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf", size)
        except Exception:
            return ImageFont.load_default()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Drawing helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def rounded_rect(draw, xy, radius, fill, outline=None, width=1):
    draw.rounded_rectangle(xy, radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=width)

def text_size(draw, text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0], bbox[3] - bbox[1]

def draw_centered_text(draw, text, font, x, y, fill):
    w, h = text_size(draw, text, font)
    draw.text((x - w // 2, y - h // 2), text, font=font, fill=fill)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
top10 = [
    ("1", "Python", "36.21%", "+5.7%", True),
    ("2", "C/C++", "13.21%", "+6.2%", True),
    ("3", "Java", "10.01%", "-5.4%", False),
    ("4", "R", "6.17%", "+1.6%", True),
    ("5", "JavaScript", "5.07%", "-3.0%", False),
    ("6", "Swift", "3.15%", "+0.8%", True),
    ("7", "C#", "3.00%", "-3.0%", False),
    ("8", "Rust", "2.98%", "-0.1%", False),
    ("9", "PHP", "2.96%", "-0.7%", False),
    ("10", "Objective-C", "2.57%", "+0.1%", True),
]

emerging = [
    ("Ada", "2.51%", "+1.1%", "Safety-critical growth"),
    ("R", "6.17%", "+1.6%", "Data-science demand"),
    ("Julia", "0.73%", "+0.4%", "Scientific computing"),
    ("Go", "0.71%", "-1.3%", "Cloud-native decline"),
    ("Kotlin", "0.90%", "-0.9%", "Android backing slipping"),
    ("Zig", "0.24%", "+0.0%", "Niche but stable"),
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main canvas
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

y = 50

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Header
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
font_title = get_font(48, bold=True)
font_sub = get_font(22)
font_tag = get_font(18)

draw.text((MARGIN, y), "PYPL Index", font=font_title, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
y += 60
draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Programming Language Popularity — April 2026", font=font_sub, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
y += 40
rounded_rect(draw, (MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 180, y + 32), 6, fill="#1E293B")
draw.text((MARGIN + 12, y + 4), "Data Report", font=font_tag, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
y += 60

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Three headline stat callouts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
stat_box_w = (W - 2 * MARGIN - 20) // 3
stat_h = 160
for idx, (label, value, context, positive) in enumerate([
    ("Python Share", "36.21%", "#1 worldwide  ·  +5.7% YoY", True),
    ("C/C++ Share", "13.21%", "#2 worldwide  ·  +6.2% YoY", True),
    ("Java Share", "10.01%", "#3 worldwide  ·  -5.4% YoY", False),
]):
    x = MARGIN + idx * (stat_box_w + 10)
    rounded_rect(draw, (x, y, x + stat_box_w, y + stat_h), 12, fill=PANEL, outline=BORDER)
    # value
    font_val = get_font(42, bold=True)
    vw, vh = text_size(draw, value, font_val)
    color = ACCENT_GREEN if positive else ACCENT_RED
    draw.text((x + (stat_box_w - vw) // 2, y + 20), value, font=font_val, fill=color)
    # label
    font_lbl = get_font(20, bold=True)
    lw, lh = text_size(draw, label, font_lbl)
    draw.text((x + (stat_box_w - lw) // 2, y + 75), label, font=font_lbl, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
    # context
    font_ctx = get_font(16)
    cw, ch = text_size(draw, context, font_ctx)
    draw.text((x + (stat_box_w - cw) // 2, y + 110), context, font=font_ctx, fill=TEXT_MUTED)

y += stat_h + 50

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section title: Top 10
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
font_sec = get_font(30, bold=True)
draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Top 10 Languages by Search Share", font=font_sec, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
y += 50

# Table header
row_h = 52
table_w = W - 2 * MARGIN
col_rank = 70
col_lang = 260
col_share = 180
col_trend = table_w - col_rank - col_lang - col_share

header_y = y
rounded_rect(draw, (MARGIN, header_y, W - MARGIN, header_y + row_h), 8, fill="#1E293B")
font_hdr = get_font(18, bold=True)
draw.text((MARGIN + 20, header_y + 14), "Rank", font=font_hdr, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((MARGIN + col_rank + 20, header_y + 14), "Language", font=font_hdr, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((MARGIN + col_rank + col_lang + 20, header_y + 14), "Share", font=font_hdr, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((MARGIN + col_rank + col_lang + col_share + 20, header_y + 14), "1-Year Trend", font=font_hdr, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
y += row_h + 4

# Table rows
font_rank = get_font(22, bold=True, mono=True)
font_lang = get_font(22, bold=True)
font_share = get_font(22, mono=True)
font_trend = get_font(20, mono=True)

for rank, lang, share, trend, positive in top10:
    row_y = y
    # subtle alternating bg
    rounded_rect(draw, (MARGIN, row_y, W - MARGIN, row_y + row_h), 8, fill=PANEL if int(rank) % 2 == 1 else BG, outline=BORDER)
    # rank
    draw.text((MARGIN + 20, row_y + 12), rank, font=font_rank, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
    # language
    draw.text((MARGIN + col_rank + 20, row_y + 12), lang, font=font_lang, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
    # share
    sw, _ = text_size(draw, share, font_share)
